summary: The proof establishes the stated strict bound for the explicit tilt. The normalized facet descriptions and affine difference formula hold for arbitrary affine product representations, without lattice vertices. Within each bin, maximal interval denominators make both interval slacks strictly positive on either lattice difference, including tied denominators. Thus only the two omitted simplex slacks can exclude the two nonzero differences from the interior; they force the claimed opposite unit separations of rho and omega. Ordering these values gives the fractional-part lower bound and the valid estimate N times 2 to the power minus (N minus 1) at most one. The final exponential factor uses exactly r selected slacks, and finitely many occupied bins give the strict inequality against the infinite positive geometric sum. The cases p=q=1, a simplex factor of dimension one, m=0, singleton fibers, facet equality, and nonlattice vertices introduce no error or gap.
